skill.name: find-replace
skill.description: Guides AI agents through find-and-replace workflows using the sd CLI, ripgrep previews, and batch replacement patterns for codebases.
skill.summary: Run safer codebase find-and-replace workflows with sd and preview steps.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, and no prompt injection was found in SKILL.md or references/advanced-patterns.md. Most static hits are Markdown formatting false positives. Several examples still intentionally run Bash commands for bulk file edits, including shell command substitution, .env* edits, and Docker volume-mounted replacements.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution passes file lists from rg or git directly to sd.
remediation.suggestion: Use safer examples with null-delimited file handling or fd execution, and require preview plus diff review before applying changes.

remediation.issue: The advanced guide includes broad replacements against .env* files.
remediation.suggestion: Remove broad .env* examples or add explicit warnings, backups, and confirmation for sensitive configuration files.

remediation.issue: The Docker example mounts the current directory and installs a package in a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a pinned trusted image or state that Docker commands require explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Several examples use broad globs that can rewrite many files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer scoped paths, single-file tests, previews, and rollback instructions before any batch replacement.

finding_verdicts.reason: The example feeds a file list from rg into sd through shell command substitution, which can rewrite many files and is fragile under shell word splitting. This is a legitimate workflow, but it is a real bulk-edit risk.
The script assigns rg output to a shell variable and iterates over it unquoted, then runs sd on each file. This can mis-handle filenames and apply broad edits unexpectedly.
The command applies sd to every path returned by git diff through shell substitution. It is intended for batch editing, but it can affect a broad and shell-expanded file set.
The command applies replacements to every staged path returned by git diff through shell substitution. This can unintentionally modify staged work if used without preview and quoting safeguards.
The command substitutes a git-generated file list into sd and rewrites those files. It is a legitimate Git workflow, but the shell expansion creates real batch-edit risk.

The Docker example mounts the current directory and runs a shell command that installs sd before editing a mounted file. This is a real external-command and workspace-modification risk even though it is documented as an example.

content.user_title: Replace Code Text Safely with sd
content.value_statement: Large codebases make text replacement risky because broad patterns can edit the wrong files. This skill provides sd-based workflows with previews, scoped file selection, and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Shows sd commands for single-file and multi-file replacements.
Uses ripgrep previews before applying broad replacements.
Documents word-boundary, capture-group, and escaping patterns.
Provides batch workflows for Git-selected and fd-selected files.
Includes examples for imports, API paths, configuration names, and cleanup tasks.
limitations: Requires the sd CLI to be installed in the user environment.
Can modify many files if patterns or globs are too broad.
Does not parse language syntax or guarantee semantic refactors.
Sensitive files require manual review before any replacement.

use_cases.title: Rename Symbols Across Source Files
use_cases.description: Preview and apply whole-word replacements for functions, variables, or constants across a scoped directory.

use_cases.title: Update Import Paths During Refactors
use_cases.description: Replace relative imports, aliases, or module names while reviewing the affected files before changes land.

use_cases.title: Plan Controlled Configuration Changes
use_cases.description: Prepare cautious replacement steps for version strings, endpoints, or configuration keys with verification after each stage.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Replacement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to preview replacing {old_text} with {new_text} in {path}. Show affected files before changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Rename a Symbol
prompt_templates.prompt: Find whole-word matches for {old_name} in {directory}. Preview replacements with {new_name}, then apply only after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Update Imports
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace import path {old_import} with {new_import} in {file_glob}. Use precise escaping and review the diff.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a staged replacement plan for {migration_goal}. Include file selection, preview commands, rollback steps, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: Replace an old feature flag name in TypeScript files.
output: A scoped list of files that contain the old feature flag.
A preview of replacements before any file changes.
A final review step that checks remaining matches and changed files.

output_examples.input: Move relative utility imports to a project alias.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies target import statements, applies precise replacements to source files, and asks for a diff review.

output_examples.input: Clean up console logging across a source directory.
output_examples.output: The workflow narrows the path, previews affected lines, removes matching statements, and verifies no unwanted matches remain.

best_practices: Preview every replacement before writing files.
Start with the smallest path or file glob that solves the task.
Review the final diff and rerun the search after applying changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad replacements from the repository root without a preview.
Do not edit sensitive configuration files without explicit approval.
Do not use regex patterns when a simple literal replacement is enough.

faq.question: What tool does this skill use?
faq.answer: It focuses on sd, a command-line replacement tool, and uses ripgrep for previews and verification.

faq.question: Can it replace sed commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows common sed patterns and their sd equivalents for simpler replacement syntax.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows that an agent may execute only with the available tool permissions and user approval rules.

faq.question: Is it safe for large refactors?
faq.answer: It can help, but broad replacements need previews, scoped paths, and final diff review.

faq.question: Can it handle regular expressions?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents capture groups, word boundaries, escaping, and multiline patterns supported by sd.

faq.question: What should users check before applying changes?
faq.answer: Users should check affected files, replacement previews, sensitive paths, and the final diff.
